title: Letter 13 — Faith Working by Love
attribution_note: Letter 13 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: Look to the Word of God, not to the crowd

pairs.en: *“My friend and companion!”*
I know that you wish to be saved in Christ. Do not look, then, at what the Christians of today are doing, but look at what the Word of God preaches and teaches.
The Christians of today, for the greater part, set themselves against Christ, and do not learn from Him — though they confess His holy name.

sections.heading: What Christ teaches, and what Christians do

pairs.en: Christ teaches us to turn from evil, but many Christians do evil. Christ teaches us to live soberly, but many Christians are given to drunkenness.
Christ teaches us to live chastely, but many Christians commit fornication and adultery.

Christ teaches us not to seize, not to steal, not to lay hands on another's goods; yet many steal — some secretly, like thieves, some openly, like violent men, and some by deceit, like the petty officials who take bribes, and will not do a man's business until they have received their fee or heard some promise of reward. To their number belong all who play at cards for money, for they play in order to win from one another. One longs to win another's money, and for this they play; and this is a sin against the tenth commandment: *“Thou shalt not covet”* [Exodus 20:17]. And whoever wins money sins also against the eighth: *“Thou shalt not steal”* [Exodus 20:15].

Christ teaches us not to avenge a wrong, but to let it pass: *“forgive, and ye shall be forgiven,”* He says [Matthew 6:14–15] — yet many Christians do not forgive, but take revenge, whether in deed or in word, and drag one another into court. And whoever does not forgive his neighbour, him God also does not forgive his sin; and so that man, whose sin is not forgiven, abides under the wrath of God.
Christ teaches us to love one another, but many Christians hate their fellow men. The apostle calls such people murderers: *“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer,”* he says [1 John 3:15].
O how many murderers there are in the world, how many thieves — as you yourself may see from what has been written above!
Christ teaches us not to judge, not to condemn; yet many Christians study nothing so much as how to gossip about their neighbours and bite them with their tongues.

Christ teaches us, from the wealth given us, to have pity on the poor and provide for them; but many Christians squander their wealth on their own fancies — on costly clothing, on building, on horses, on carriages, on rich tables and costly wines, and the like.

Christ teaches us to be merciful; but many Christians, when they see a poor man, say shamelessly: “What is his need to me?” They see the naked and will not clothe him; they see the homeless and will not give him a roof; they see the hungry and will not feed him; they see the stranger and will not take him into their home — and so forth. Instead, they pour out their wealth on indulgences that are contrary to God and ruinous to themselves.
Christ teaches us to seek the kingdom of heaven; but many Christians seek only to be glorified and enriched in this world, and carry themselves as though they wished to live here for ever.
Christ teaches us not to speak filthily; but many Christians do not fear, with the very lips wherewith they call upon the holy and fearful name of God, to utter all manner of foul and unclean words.

Christ teaches us to pray often; but many Christians spend all their time in revelry, or at feasts, or at the gaming-table, or following the hounds, or in empty, idle, shameful and lawless talk, or in some other vanity.

O how Christ is held in contempt among so many Christians! For they do not listen to Him, though He is their God, their Lord and King, the One who feeds them and clothes them; though He suffered for them and died, and shed His Blood for them, and opened to them the eternal kingdom, and called them to it, and calls them still through His holy Word, through preachers and teachers. For a son despises his father when he will not listen to him, and a servant his master when he does not carry out his commands; and so Christians, despising the commandments of Christ, despise Christ Himself who gave them.

O ungrateful Christians! Is this the honour we ought to render to Christ, who for our sake humbled Himself, and endured agony, and wept, and suffered reviling, mockery, spitting, the stripping of His garments, wounds, the cross and death upon it? Is this the thanksgiving we ought to render Him?
He did not spare even Himself for our sake — and yet we spare our money, given us by Him, and grudge to give it to those who ask in His name.

He gave Himself over for our sake to wounds, to crucifixion and to death upon the cross, that we might be saved — and for His sake we cannot bear so much as an insulting word, but either wound with our tongues, as with arrows, those who have offended us, repelling injury with injury and evil with evil, or else fill the courts with venomous slanders.

So greatly did He honour and love us, His enemies, that He did not refuse to die for us — and we dishonour Him, our Benefactor, who so honoured and loved us, by our evil deeds. Is this what our faith requires of us, and our confession of His name? Is this the thanksgiving rendered to a Benefactor? Is this the honour due to a King? Is this the obedience due to a Lord? Is this the love due to the One who loves us?

O woe! O delusion! O how sin has gathered strength! How scandal has spread! How the world's allure has grown! How everywhere Satan has stretched out his nets, and catches poor souls, as a fisherman catches fish — now with the net of covetousness, now with the net of vainglory! O how, hour by hour, the fruit of the seed of the Word of God dwindles; how the tares multiply; how the wheat diminishes; how wickedness waxes! True godliness grows scarce, and hypocrisy abounds; Christians grow scarce, and hypocrites multiply!

sections.heading: A tree is known by its fruit

pairs.en: *“Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good.* *He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God,”* says the apostle [3 John 1:11].

By its fruit a tree is known, and an apple by its taste, and an herb by its scent; and a Christian is known by faith and love, as a rose by its beauty and its fragrance. *“For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love,”* says the holy Paul [Galatians 5:6]. If this is so — as indeed it is — then where is one to look for a true Christian, when almost everyone seeks only his own, and not his neighbour's good?

sections.heading: Every good deed flows from love

pairs.en: Faith looks upon Christ crucified and risen, and acknowledges Him as its Redeemer and Saviour; and how can it not love Him, its Redeemer and Saviour, who has redeemed those who believe in Him from eternal death and grants them eternal life? If it loves Him, how can it not keep His commandments? And Christ commands Christians to *“love one another”* [John 15:17].

You love Christ — and so you do not wish to offend Him, and fear to offend Him, for offence is contrary to love. You do not wish to offend Him — and so you must not break His commandments. You fear to offend your father — and so you carry out his orders. You do not wish to offend your friend — and so you do what pleases him. You honour authority — and so you obey it. You see, then, that upon love for Christ there follows obedience to Christ; upon obedience, the keeping of His commandment; and upon the keeping of His commandment, love for one's neighbour.

Christ says: *“These things I command you, that ye love one another”* [John 15:17]. And if you love your neighbour, will you despise him in his need? How can you not clothe the naked man whom you love? How can you not feed the hungry man whom you love? How can you not take into your home and set at table the one whom you love? How can you not visit the sick man, and the one who sits in prison, whom you love? How can you not comfort the sorrowful man whom you love? How could you wish to wound with a word the one whom you love? How could you wish to deceive and ensnare the one whom you love? How could you wish to slander and condemn the one whom you love? How could you wish to seize the goods of the one whom you love? How could you not wish every good upon the one whom you love? In a word: the one you love, you will neither wish nor do any evil to; and you will wish and do every good for the one you love.

You see that from love every good deed proceeds. If, then, you love Christ as your Redeemer, and do not wish to offend Him, love your neighbour without hypocrisy, that you may not offend Christ your Saviour — for Christ has commanded you to love your neighbour, as was said. And if you would love your neighbour as you ought, then do not wish upon him what you do not wish upon yourself, and wish upon him and do for him what you wish for yourself. For this is the very nature of love.

See, then, what a Christian is, and by what he is known: by faith and by love. And where there is no love, there is no faith either; and where there is no faith, there is no Christianity — for a Christian cannot exist without faith.

Here, then, is the reason, set out before you, for which I wrote at the beginning: do not look at what the Christians of today do, but look at what the Word of God preaches and teaches. For one takes his example from another, and is led into scandal; and so scandal and sin multiply, and godliness diminishes, and true Christians grow scarce, and hypocrisy enters in — and upon hypocrisy follows eternal ruin. There is your gift!
Be saved in Christ!
